threads.author: rosa
threads.title: Hello — I brought ten years of notices with me
threads.message:
I am on the community centre committee, which shares this board with the club since the two of us gave up pretending we had different members.

I have spent the last month moving about a decade of notices, minutes and event listings onto here from a website that only I could edit. It took three sittings and most of it was me deciding what was worth keeping.

The answer, if it helps anyone: minutes, yes. Photos, yes. Every "hall booked Tuesday" from 2016, no.

threads.author: newcomer
threads.title: Just found this, working out if it fits us
threads.message:
Hi. I help run a running club two towns over — about ninety members, currently a chat group and a spreadsheet of race entries.

Somebody in our group sent me your fixtures forum as an example of what we should be doing. Is this a lot of work to keep going, honestly?

replies.author: admin
replies.message: Honestly: the first month is work and after that it is less than the chat was. The thing that decides it is not the software, it is whether two or three of you will post without being asked. If you have those people it runs itself. If you do not, it will be quiet and you will blame the tool.

replies.author: rosa
replies.message: Second that, and one practical thing: do not migrate the chat. Leave it running and start the board for the things worth keeping — race entries, results, minutes. The chat gets quieter on its own.

threads.title: Winter tournament: brackets, rules and what you win
threads.message:
Sixteen teams of three, double elimination, seeded by nothing at all because none of us know what we are doing.

Rules, such as they are:

- Teams of three. One sub allowed, named before your first match.
- Best of three until the semis, best of five after.
- **Two under-18 places per team maximum**, and they play the early slots only.
- The prize is a trophy that Tomás is making out of an old cup we found in the clubhouse. It is genuinely hideous.

Sign up by replying with your three names. Fourteen teams so far.

threads.author: noelle
threads.title: How subs work, in plain English
threads.message:
Pinned because I answer this eleven times every January.

**Adult playing** covers the league registration, insurance, pitch hire and referees. It is the biggest one and roughly two-thirds of it goes straight back out to the league before we see it.

**Adult social** is the same membership without the playing registration. You get a vote at the AGM, the clubhouse, and every event we run.

**Juvenile** covers a child for a full season, including the camp week at a reduced rate. **Family** covers everybody in a household and works out cheaper from the second child.

**Supporters** is the optional one on top. It is not a membership — it is people choosing to put a few euro a month in, and it is currently paying for the juvenile jerseys.

Nobody has ever been turned away for not being able to pay. If that is you, message me and it is dealt with quietly and nobody else knows.

replies.message: Renewed three lads from the over-35s by forwarding this to them. None of them had realised the social one existed.

replies.author: noelle
replies.message: Nine of the thirty-one renewed in a week and one of them is back playing. Worth writing.

threads.author: admin
threads.title: People were getting logged out every couple of hours. Fixed.
threads.message:
Four people told me they were being logged out during the day and I could not reproduce it on my own account, which is the worst kind of bug.

Cause: I put a second web container in when the board got busy on match days, and the two of them did not share the same signing secret. A session made by one was gibberish to the other, so every second request looked like a stranger.

Same secret on both, redeployed, gone. Writing it down because it took me two evenings and the symptom points nowhere near the cause.

replies.author: paudie
replies.message: I thought I was doing something wrong and had stopped mentioning it. That is the real cost of a bug like that.

replies.author: rosa
replies.message: Same, and I had started keeping the tab open all day so I would not have to log in again.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: That is exactly the behaviour that hides it — the people it affects stop reporting it and work around it. Please always tell me, even when you assume it is you.

replies.author: vex
replies.message: Two containers on match day is a nice problem for a club board to have, in fairness.

threads.author: rosa
threads.title: Search finds nothing for a thread I am looking straight at
threads.message:
Searching for "shoebox" gives me nothing, and the shoebox thread is right there on the noticeboard with my name on it.

Everything else about the site is completely normal. It is only search.

replies.author: admin
replies.message:
That will be me. I moved the board to the new server on Sunday and restored from a dump, and the search index does not always come across in one — the posts are all there, the thing that makes them findable is not.

Running the reindex now. It works through the whole board in the background, so it will start finding things again gradually rather than all at once.

replies.author: rosa
replies.message: Shoebox thread is back. So are the minutes from 2019, which I could not find last week either and had assumed I had imagined.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: Ninety thousand posts in about twelve minutes. Everything is findable again, including the things you had given up on.

replies.author: mira
replies.message: Worth knowing that search covers the old parish notices too. I found a 2017 hall booking argument that I would rather have left buried.

threads.author: paudie
threads.title: Cannot log in on the phone, grand on the laptop
threads.message: Same password. Works on the laptop every time, fails on the phone every time. I have typed it slowly. I have typed it very slowly.

replies.author: moderator
replies.message: Is the phone putting a capital on the first letter? It does that in the username box and the username is not the problem, the capital is.

replies.author: paudie
replies.message: It is putting a capital on it.

replies.author: paudie
replies.message: I am in. Twenty-five years of technology and I am beaten by an automatic capital letter.

replies.author: moderator
replies.message: You are the fourth. It is the single most common thing anyone asks me here.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: Fourth is enough. Names are matched without case now, so the capital does not matter any more.

replies.author: frank
replies.message: A support thread that ends with the software changing is a good day for everybody.

threads.author: cormac
threads.title: Is there an app?
threads.message: Not complaining, the site is fine on the phone. Just asking whether there is an app I am missing.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: There is not, and there will not be. What there is: add it to your home screen from the browser menu and it opens like one, full screen, no address bar. That gets you 95% of an app for none of the maintenance.

replies.author: cormac
replies.message: Did that. It is an app now as far as I am concerned.

replies.author: bernie
replies.message: Somebody should put those five words in the pinned post because I did not know you could do that.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: Added, with a screenshot for both kinds of phone.

threads.author: bernie
threads.title: My notifications have gone quiet
threads.message:
I used to get an email when the U12 thread got a reply and I have had none for about a fortnight. The thread is definitely getting replies.

Have I turned something off by accident?

replies.author: moderator
replies.message: Check the subscription on the thread first — it is at the top of the thread and it will say "watching" or "not watching". A reply from a phone sometimes gets sent with the box unticked.

replies.author: bernie
replies.message: It says not watching. I did not do that on purpose.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: You did, though not knowingly — replying with "subscribe" unticked replaces the old setting. It is a bad default and I have changed it: replying now leaves an existing subscription alone.

replies.author: bernie
replies.message: Back to normal, and I now know what that box does after a year of ignoring it.

replies.author: mairead
replies.message: Two other parents have said the same thing this month. That change will save me a lot of "did you not see the thread".

threads.author: sam
threads.title: How do I turn the emails off without leaving?
threads.message:
I am on here every day. I do not need to be told by email that a thread I read an hour ago has a reply.

I do want the ones about my own account and the fixture cancellations. Is that a setting or is it all or nothing?

replies.author: moderator
replies.message: It is a setting, in your account under notifications, and it splits about six ways. Turn off thread replies, leave the account and announcement ones on.

replies.author: sam
replies.message: Found it. Six switches and I have flicked four. Perfect.

replies.author: petra
replies.message: I did the opposite last month — turned everything on and it is far too much. Somewhere in the middle is the answer and it took me a while to find it.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: The middle is going to be the default for new accounts from now on. Nobody's first week should be forty emails.

threads.author: dev
threads.title: Photos upload fine and then are not on the post
threads.message:
Progress bar goes all the way, post saves, and there is no photo on it. Happened with about sixty from Saturday.

Started after the server move. Working on a laptop and on the phone, so it is not me.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: Photos are resized in the background rather than while you wait — that is why a hundred of them do not lock the page up. So this is almost always the background worker not running rather than the upload failing. Checking the tasks screen now.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: The worker is not in the new setup at all. It never got copied across in the move. That is entirely my fault and nothing is lost — everything queued is still queued.

replies.author: dev
replies.message: All sixty appeared within a minute of each other just now. That was alarming and then delightful.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: That is the queue draining. The reminder emails and the membership expiries run on the same thing, which explains two other small mysteries this week.

replies.author: noelle
replies.message: It explains why three renewals did not expire on time. I had assumed I had done something wrong.

threads.author: kev
threads.title: Can somebody be stopped from opening six threads a day without banning them?
threads.message:
One person, breaking no rule, being perfectly pleasant, and opening five or six threads a day in Buy, sell and swap where one would do.

I would like them to be able to reply and not to open new ones, in that one forum. Is that a thing or am I inventing it?

replies.author: admin
replies.message: It is a thing. Permissions resolve per group per forum, so you make a group with "post threads" off and "post replies" on, put them in it, and apply it to that one forum. They will not notice anywhere else on the board.

replies.author: kev
replies.message: Did not know it went per forum. That is exactly the shape of the problem.

replies.author: moderator
replies.message: Talk to them first though. Nine times out of ten "you are posting a lot, could you do one thread" works and nobody has to be quietly restricted.

replies.author: kev
replies.message: Talked to them. They had no idea and were mortified. One thread now, updated as things sell. No permissions needed.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: That is the right order to do it in and I should have said so first.

threads.author: donal
threads.title: The board on a phone at a pitch with one bar of signal
threads.message:
Standing in a field in Ennis trying to check whether the second game was 12 or 12:30, on one bar, in the rain.

It loaded. That is the whole feedback. I have used club websites that would not have loaded on the wifi at home and this one came up in a field.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: That is the thing I care most about and almost nobody ever mentions, so thank you. Pages are plain HTML first and the clever bits come after — which is why it works on one bar.

replies.author: mairead
replies.message: Twelve. It was 12. And I know because I checked it in the same field.

replies.author: zoe
replies.message: The old site needed the app to do anything and the app needed a signal. Two seasons of standing on a wall holding a phone in the air.

threads.author: pixel
threads.title: Dark mode, and can we have the club colours in it
threads.message:
Half the Tuesday crowd is on this at eleven at night and the board is very white.

Also, and I say this with love: the default look is fine, but a club with green and white on the crest could have green and white on the site.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: There is a picker at the bottom of every page and it takes a click, no account needed. Try the dark one now and tell me if the greens are wrong on your screen.

replies.author: pixel
replies.message: Found it. Four options. Two of them are genuinely lovely and one of them looks like a raid interface, which I did not expect from a club website.

replies.author: wraith
replies.message: The raid one is the only one I will use and I will hear nothing about it.

replies.author: siobhan
replies.message: And the club colours are in the crest at the top, which is the compromise I am happy with. The whole site in green and white was tried in 2011 and it was unreadable.

replies.author: bram
replies.message: The picker sticking without an account is the good bit. My mother reads the fixtures on here and will never make an account, and she has it on the big-text one.

threads.author: mairead
threads.title: A calendar view would be lovely
threads.message:
Everything is in Events and it is all findable, but a parent with children in three teams is reading four threads to work out one Saturday.

A month at a glance would save me the twelve messages I get every Friday.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: Fair, and it is not there. What is there today: subscribe to a team's threads and the emails arrive as things change. That is not a calendar and I am not pretending it is.

replies.author: bernie
replies.message: Seconding hard. Three children, three teams, and I keep a paper calendar on the fridge because of this exact thing.

replies.author: nova
replies.message: Same on our side for a completely different reason — the ranked block and the raid night are fixed times and new people cannot see them at a glance anywhere.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: That is two very different groups asking for the same screen, which is usually the sign it is worth building. On the list, honestly rather than politely.

replies.author: mairead
replies.message: Honestly rather than politely is all I ask of any committee.

threads.author: dara
threads.title: A prefix for a called-off fixture
threads.message:
We have Fixture, Sign-up and Result. When a game is off I edit the title to start with "OFF —" and it looks like shouting.

A grey "Called off" prefix would do the job and would be visible from the forum list without opening anything.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: Prefixes are a screen in the admin panel, so this is about a minute of work rather than a feature. Adding it tonight, scoped to Events so it does not clutter the rest of the board.

replies.author: marty
replies.message: Can it be a loud colour rather than grey? The whole point is that people see it at a glance from the phone in the car park.

replies.author: dara
replies.message: Fine. Loud it is. I withdraw grey.

replies.author: gerry
replies.message: I will be the one using it most and I would like it in red, thank you.

threads.author: nova
threads.title: Sign-up threads should close themselves
threads.message:
Every week somebody signs up for the Sunday block on the Sunday evening, after the teams are drawn, and then wonders why they are not on one.

If a sign-up thread could lock itself at a time I set when I post it, that solves it without me having to remember to lock fourteen threads.

replies.author: tinker
replies.message: Same for the raid roster. I lock it manually on Monday nights and I have forgotten twice.

replies.author: olu
replies.message: And the five-a-side. Three of us are describing one feature, which I think is the point of this forum.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: It does not exist. What does: locking a thread is one click for a moderator, and all three of you are moderators of your own corner already. Not a solution, an admission.

replies.author: nova
replies.message: An honest "no, and here is the workaround" is worth more than a maybe. Locking manually it is.

threads.author: olu
threads.title: Could Events be the first thing you see?
threads.message:
Announcements is at the top because it is important, but it changes twice a month. Events changes every day and it is what almost everybody is actually here for.

Not a complaint about the order. A question about what a first-time visitor sees.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: The order is a number on each forum in the admin panel and I can change it in ten seconds. The question is whether Announcements stops getting read if it moves down.

replies.author: siobhan
replies.message: It will stop getting read. That is not a guess — it is what happened on the old site when the notices went below the fold.

replies.author: kev
replies.message: Compromise: leave the order alone and make the front page show the newest posts across everything. Then the busy forum is at the top by being busy.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: That already exists, it is just not the landing page. Making it the landing page for logged-in members and leaving the forum list for everybody else. Trying it for a fortnight.

replies.author: olu
replies.message: Two days in and the Thursday sign-up has four more people than usual. Small thing, real difference.

threads.author: siobhan
threads.title: What the staff will and will not do
threads.message:
Written down because "the moderators" being a vague and slightly frightening idea does nobody any good.

**We will:** take down anything about a child that a parent is not happy with, immediately and without argument. Remove spam. Lock a thread that has stopped being a conversation. Have a private word before we do anything public.

**We will not:** delete a post because it disagrees with the committee. Take sides in an argument about a referee. Remove a complaint about how the club is run — those stay up, including the ones that are unfair, because a board where the criticism disappears is worth nothing.

**Who we are:** two administrators, two super moderators, and four moderators who each look after a corner of the board. Names are on the staff page and every one of us is a volunteer with a day job.

If you think we got something wrong, say so. There is a report button on every post and it comes to all of us, not just the person you are annoyed with.

replies.author: frank
replies.message: The bit about complaints staying up is the one that matters and it is the one most clubs would quietly leave out.

replies.author: rosa
replies.message: It has been tested twice since this was posted and held both times, which is the only reason anybody believes it.

replies.author: moderator
replies.message: Worth adding: a report is not an accusation. Half of what I get is "this is probably fine but you should see it", and that is exactly the right use of it.

threads.author: mairead
threads.title: Photos of children: the rule, and why it is not up for discussion
threads.message:
One rule, in three parts.

1. **No photograph of a child goes on this board unless their parent has ticked the box on the membership form.** Not "unless they objected". Ticked.
2. **Any parent can ask for any photo to come down, at any time, without giving a reason**, and it will be gone inside an hour.
3. **No full names of under-18s** beside a photograph. First name only, and only if the parent is happy with that too.

This is not the committee being nervous. It is the safeguarding policy we are required to have and it is also, separately, just the right way to behave.

Locked because it is a policy rather than a discussion. Questions to me or to the welfare officer, any time.

threads.author: dara
threads.title: Why every new account's first post is held
threads.message:
A new member posted on Saturday, saw "waiting for approval", and messaged me thinking they had done something wrong.

They had not. Every brand new account has its first post held until somebody looks at it, and it is almost always approved within the hour.

It exists because it is the single most effective thing we do against spam. The bots that get through registration still cannot get a link onto the board, because a person reads the first thing they write.

replies.author: moderator
replies.message: And the wording on the screen is now much friendlier than it was, because that member was the third person to think they were in trouble.

replies.author: admin
replies.message: It costs the staff about four clicks a week. It has stopped, at a rough count, three hundred spam posts.

replies.author: kev
replies.message: The queue is the least glamorous screen on the board and it is the one that keeps this place readable.

replies.author: rook
replies.message: Mine was held and approved in about twenty minutes, and the message explained why. No complaints at all.

threads.author: admin
threads.title: The spam wave last month, and what actually stopped it
threads.message:
About nine hundred registration attempts over four days. Roughly thirty got as far as writing a post. Writing it down because two other clubs locally got the same wave the same week.

**Did not work:** the hidden field that bots are supposed to fill in. Whatever was driving this filled the form like a browser, because it was one.

**Worked:** the registration question. One line, specific to the club, that you cannot answer by reading the page — ours asks what colour the away jerseys were before the change. Attempts went from about two hundred a day to under five.

**Worked quietly:** holding first posts. The thirty that got through never became visible, so the board never looked spammed, which matters more than the raw number.

Cost to real people: two members emailed to say the question was confusing. Both got in the same evening.

replies.author: siobhan
replies.message: The "never looked spammed" part is underrated. A board that looks unmoderated attracts more of it and puts off the members you want.

replies.author: rosa
replies.message: The community centre board got the same wave. Question worked for us too — ours asks what is across the road from the hall.

replies.author: vex
replies.message: Do not make the question too clever. Ours was too clever for a fortnight and three real people failed it.

replies.author: kev
replies.message: What do we do about the one that got through last week into Buy, sell and swap? It is reported and still sitting there.

replies.author: moderator
replies.message: It is in the queue and I have deliberately left it for whoever is on next, so they can see what one looks like before it disappears.

threads.author: moderator
threads.title: Match threads get heated. Where is the line?
threads.message:
Saturday's thread had four posts about the referee that I would not want the referee to read, and one about an opposition player by name that I took down.

I am fairly sure I got the second one right and much less sure about the first four. Nobody swore. Nobody was personal about anybody in this club.

Where do people think the line is, before I have to decide it on my own at eleven at night?

replies.author: siobhan
replies.message: Named opposition player, especially an under-18, is over it every single time. You were right.

replies.author: marty
replies.message: On referees: they are volunteers who get abused for a living and half of them are members of clubs like ours. "The referee had a shocker" is fine. Anything about the person is not.

replies.author: paudie
replies.message: I wrote one of the four. Reading it back I would not have said it to his face, which is probably the whole test.

replies.author: deco
replies.message: That is the best rule anybody has put in this thread. Would you say it to their face at the club bar afterwards.

replies.author: moderator
replies.message: Taking that as the line and putting it in the pinned post. It is one sentence and everyone will remember it.

replies.author: dara
replies.message: And I will keep writing the match reports so there is somewhere sensible for the frustration to go. Half of it is people with nowhere to put a bad Saturday.

threads.author: moderator
threads.title: How do you handle a member who is technically fine and exhausting?
threads.message:
Not a rule-breaker. Never rude. Replies to every thread within a minute, at length, usually restating what the post above said.

Three people have quietly told me they have stopped posting because of it. I have no rule that covers this and I am not sure I want one.

replies.author: siobhan
replies.message: Talk to them. A private message that says "you are one of the most active people here and I need to ask you to leave some room" works more often than the internet expects. I have done it four times and it worked three.

replies.author: vex
replies.message:
And the fourth?

Asking seriously — the failure case is the one nobody writes down, and it is the one I would want to know about before trying it.

replies.author: siobhan
replies.message: The fourth left in a temper and said a few things about me in the shop. The board was better for it and I would still do it again. It is not free.

replies.author: moderator
replies.message: Sent one this morning. Will report back.

replies.author: moderator
replies.message: Reporting back: went well. They were mortified, which I felt bad about, and have visibly pulled back without going quiet. Recommended, with the warning attached.

replies.author: kev
replies.message: The same conversation works for the six-threads-a-day thing. It is remarkable how often the answer is "nobody has ever told them".
